title: What do we think? Top left is the one that got ROASTED 🔥 yesterday. Bottom right is my best attempt to improve. This pixel art filter is 100% free forever, open source, runs locally, available to use in browser via wasm.
author: gametorch

comments.author: name_was_taken
comments.body:
2 things are true:

It's still not nearly as good as properly done pixel art.

It's already way better than I could do.

replies.author: Physical-Mission-867
replies.body: Just curious, but could you elaborate on "properly done pixel art"?

replies.author: name_was_taken
replies.body: In this case, their solution to having the outline be patchy was to make it extra thick.  So instead of a pixel art character, it looks like a sticker.  A real artist would work on the outline specifically to make it look right, but this automated process can't really do that.

comments.author: InternationalOne2449
comments.body: One day i'll be able to make a game with just prompting. No coding or programing.

comments.author: joanmave
comments.body: Looks better. The graininess in the eyes and some noise between the solid colors of the hair and the outline, and you got something many could use. Maybe the same way k means can be used to reassign the palette it could be use to paint rogue pixels.

comments.author: joanmave
comments.body: On another note, I did not so long  ago code to clean pixel art generated by AI, my approach was to transform AI pixels into true pixels by first identifying a grid that could separate cleanly every AI pixel into a “cell”. This way I have a workable representation of the intended pixels and then I can apply k means and stuff. The reason is that AI pixel are is not pixel perfect, in fact is very bad. Pixels that are not square, vertical and horizontal pixel arrangement that are not perfectly vertical or horizontal. This throws off any naive interpolation or aliasing.

comments.author: LopsidedLobster2100
comments.body: Nice thing about AI is that it only needs to fool the person generating it. A low res 3d model is not a sprite. None of these models would work well in a 2d environment
